label: Non-concrete item simply prior to an actual concretum
definition: SomeSimplyPriorNonConcrete m w PriorSimply holds when there are distinct y and x such that y is simply prior to x, x is concrete and exists at w, and y is not concrete. Ordinary meaning: something that is not a concrete thing comes first, absolutely, before a concrete thing. Example: the number two, or the Form of the Good, prior to a concrete thing. It does not say the prior item is absent, and the priority is not temporal.
note: Analyst framework definition of a rival position; attribution deferred. Motivated by Platonism about priority. Rival of SimplyPriorIsActualConcreteGround on the same Profile, world and PriorSimply. Stronger than the negation: it fixes that the concreteness clause fails. PriorSimply keeps its recorded sense (DEF-SIMPLE-PRIORITY).
